known_costs: Committing a pointer forfeits the metric's width-only free pass on an 8-byte scalar (head::elide_tail_bytes_pipe).
Committing a byte forfeits the same free pass one level down (tar::check_compressed_archive, GT _Bool).

A value that is not a pointer at all can be committed: coreutils cp -O0 sub_f8ce holds a NAME_MAX limit in a slot the body also steps by one byte, and `long v6; v6 = 0xff;` becomes `char *v6; v6 = (char *)0xff;` with `if (v2 > (long)v6)`. That particular row is value-preserving (every widening and comparison picks up an explicit cast) but reads worse. It is NOT true of the class as a whole: diffutils diff -O0 sub_2180a (review round 2) showed the same shape printing a fabricated string literal -- see wrong_output_found. The earlier blanket 'verified semantically equivalent' claim for this class was wrong and is withdrawn. (Re-checked on b6d572c26: `long v6; v6 = 0xff;` in both the pre-fix and the fixed build with the option on, so this row no longer reproduces.)

`unsigned char *` is not protected by the refine guard: the vote is read against the type IN FLIGHT, so `char *` lands where `uint1 *` would only have arrived by later propagation (decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/protoorder_x86_64: `int callee(unsigned char *a0,int a1)` -> `int callee(char *a0,int a1)`). A `FILE *` in the same signature is untouched.

The signedness can move the OTHER way as a knock-on: a correct `char *` arrives as `unsigned char *`. No 444-slice project carries it; measured on dash -O0, 13 lines in 7 functions (4 signatures: sub_68c3, sub_128e1, sub_1295d, sub_155e7), 2 of those bodies losing a character literal (`*a0 != '_'` -> `*a0 != 0x5f`). Against it in the same binary: 23 lines forward to `char *` and 4 `strcmp` casts dropped.

LAYOUT PRECISION (measured, 8 binaries / ~2,300 functions): no `struct_N *` declaration ever moves (1,286 in both arms); 3 typed-pointer declarations become `char *`, all of them e2fsck::ext2fs_bitcount, through the in-flight refine guard; and wide field reads rendered through an indexed character pointer go 1,202 -> 1,204, both lines in e2fsck::sub_678f8's group descriptor. See layout_precision and analysis.md.

The offset rule declines two correct idioms with the shape of a field: skipping a string's first character (`p + 1`) and writing a number backwards from `buf + 20` (gnulib umaxtostr). See offset_rule_round5.cost.

wrong_output_found.symptom: with `charptr on`, a numeric constant printed as a string literal read out of an ELF loader table

witness.function: an iconv loop; the 5th iconv argument is outbytesleft = 0x1000, the size of `char v1[4104]`
witness.section: .dynsym (0x400..0x10d8); the bytes at 0x1000 are b'5\x00', the st_name field of a symbol-table entry

wrong_output_found.root_cause: NOT charptr's own vote. The JSON `variables[]` is byte-identical in both arms -- v2 is `char *` with or without the option -- and only the CONSTANT's rendering moves. The literal comes from `PrintC::pushPtrCharConstant`, whose only gate is `Scope::isReadOnly`, and `ElfFormat::section_bits` painted `.dynsym`/`.dynstr`/`.gnu.hash`/`.rela.*` read-only because they are SHF_ALLOC and not SHF_WRITE. charptr commits the NEIGHBOURING slot (stack@-4192, ev=byte, the correct iconv outbuf) and that reorders the fold enough for the constant to pick up the `char *` its destination already had.
wrong_output_found.fix: strict fix in the same PR: the dynamic loader's tables lose the read-only bit (kuna-analysis/src/loader/format/elf.rs, is_loader_table), and `operand_refs` stops accepting a scalar that lands in one -- the same reason its .got/.plt exclusion exists.

The guard only widens the no-change set: functions byte-identical in both arms go 10,624 -> 10,635.

layout_precision.method: 8 whole binaries, both arms of the same build, decompile-all over every function, variables keyed on their storage comment so renumbering cannot fake a move.
layout_precision.typed_pointer_to_char_detail: all three are e2fsck::ext2fs_bitcount (unsigned int *a0 plus its two stack copies); the refine guard reads the type in flight, so a pointee that only arrives by later propagation is not there to protect. Upstream declares it `int ext2fs_bitcount(const void *addr, int nbytes)`.
layout_precision.char_to_something_else_detail: four functions, all to unsigned char */uint1 * -- the signedness knock-on already recorded in known_costs (crond sub_caa6, e2fsck sub_51c76, ls sub_7920 and sub_7d70).
layout_precision.struct_pointer_declarations: 1286 off -> 1286 on: no synthesized struct_N * is ever replaced by char *.
layout_precision.wide_field_reads_through_an_indexed_poin: 1202 off -> 1204 on (+2), both in e2fsck::sub_678f8, where v11 = ext2fs_group_desc(...) commits and *(unsigned short *)(v11 + 0x1e) prints as *(unsigned short *)&v11[0x1e]; the same statement's zero store splits into two byte stores, value-preserving and worse to read.
layout_precision.crond_dirent_control: cronie crond -O0 sub_6715 is byte-identical in both arms after the offset guard.

offset_rule_round5.what: Follow-up to #695 (post-merge review). kuna_charptr::classify_use's PTRADD arm now reads the index: a constant non-zero index is a field offset (ForwardOffset), index zero is identity, and a one-byte step taken from an already-offset value forwards without counting. Only a computed index from the base is character evidence. Before, a constant PTRADD counted as a byte step, so `&d->d_name[0]` on a `struct dirent *` -- an INT_ADD while `d` was an integer, PTRADD(d, 0x13, 1) once an earlier fold typed it void * -- committed the base to char *.
counterexamples_fixed: dpkg-trigger -O2 sub_58d0: (char *a0) on main with charptr on -> (void *a0)
gcc -O0 / -O2 of `for (p = d->d_name; *p; p++)` on struct dirent *: (char *a0) -> (void *a0); stage controls #9/#10
offset_rule_round5.cost: Two correct idioms have exactly the shape of a field and are now declined with it. (1) Skipping a string's first character before the first read (`p + 1`): coreutils realpath path_prefix, env scan_varname, printf print_esc, od -O2 sub_4270 keep void * with the option on; stage control #11 pins path_prefix. (2) Writing a number backwards from the end of a caller's buffer, gnulib umaxtostr/imaxtostr/inttostr (`p = buf + 20; *p = 0; *--p = ...`): tar -O0 sub_54bde/sub_54d1c/sub_54e5a (and sysinttostr above them), ls -O2 sub_12680/sub_12720, sort -O2 sub_e120/sub_e1b0/sub_e200 keep `void *buf` and, as in the default arm, get a separate `char *v2` for the moving cursor instead of reusing the parameter.
